questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: What is freshness in a data backbone?
options: The size of the newest index generation
The time from a source change to its effect being visible to queries
The number of documents parsed per hour
The share of cache entries still valid

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: How does a stage compute its lag?
options: Now minus the maximum source timestamp it has processed

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: Lag doubles every hour though the SLA has not yet been breached. Why alert anyway?
options: A growing lag means the consumer is falling behind the producer

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: A full index rebuild takes six hours. What is wrong with the index at publish time?
options: It is already six hours stale when it is born
It has no ACL fields yet

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: How should a rebuild avoid staleness at publish?
options: Pause all ingestion during the build
Snapshot at a recorded timestamp, keep serving the live index, and replay events since the snapshot before swapping
Build twice as fast on larger machines

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: A revocation at 09:10 takes effect at 09:32 against a 5-minute SLA because compaction locked the segment. What is the correct follow-up?
options: Move the index to larger hardware
Couple compaction windows to SLA alerts and track an error budget

The mean rank of all returned results
The reciprocal rank of the first clicked or cited result, averaged
The number of sessions per query

options: An address for the stage whose output changed
Proof the query mix is seasonal
Evidence to rebuild the golden set

questions.question: What does a rising re-query rate usually mean?
options: First answers are failing and users rephrase
The cache TTL is too long

questions.question: After a chunker deploy, reranker top-1 p50 falls from 0.81 to 0.74 and post-dedupe candidates halve. What is the diagnosis?
options: The new chunker emits near-duplicates that dedupe collapses, starving the reranker

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: What is a golden query set?
options: Every query from the last quarter
Queries with the highest reranker scores
A versioned set of queries with adjudicated relevant documents, stratified by class

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: What is the correct acceptance rule for an index change?
options: The average metric must improve overall
No query class may regress beyond its threshold
At least half the queries must improve

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: A planted document must rank first for `canary refund policy xq9` and is queried every minute. What does a miss detect?
options: Live index corruption, ACL regression, or a serving bug

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: How does a freshness canary work?
options: A planted document is updated hourly and its time-to-visibility is measured
A judge scores the freshness of answers
The index is rebuilt every hour
Logs are sampled for recent timestamps

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: A team tunes BM25 parameters until the golden set passes. What is the safeguard?
options: Use more decimal places in metrics
A held-out slice never used for tuning, only final validation

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: What is the standard fix for golden-set rot?
options: Quarterly review plus a rule that every incident contributes its queries
